    Gravis Robotics is a high-growth Series A start-up backed by SoftBank, bringing Physical AI to the construction industry, turning heavy construction machines into autonomous robots. 

    Gravis began as an ETH Zurich spin-out, and our unique combination of learning-based automation and augmented remote control lets one operator safely conduct a fleet of earthmoving machines in a gamified environment. 

    Backed by deep robotics research and now deployed across multiple countries with leading construction and equipment partners, our team is rapidly growing to bring this technology to a trillion-dollar industry. 

    The Gravis RACK is a machine-agnostic retrofit kit that adds autonomy to excavators and wheel loaders from 10 to 100+ tonnes: LiDAR and camera sensing, GNSS RTK, networking hardware and rugged edge compute that works offline. Paired with the Slate tablet and our Copilot software, it lets an operator run a machine manually, with AI assistance, or fully autonomously.  Increasingly, we also build custom hardware to adapt our machines for highly specialized, robust applications beyond traditional excavation. 


    About the Job

    The autonomy team at Gravis architects autonomous behaviors for different tasks, e.g. different types of excavation or truck loading. This role owns the architecture that lets those behaviors live in the same software stack as opposed to creating one SW stack per behavior. You'll be responsible for how tasks are decomposed and orchestrated, for the interfaces between, and for the software quality. We are looking for a senior roboticist with C++ and Python expertise and high standards for software quality, who can make clear, pragmatic architectural calls that let the system grow without losing stability.


    What you'll do

    Architecture

  • Own the task-level architecture shared across our autonomous behaviors

  • Define clear module boundaries and responsibilities between behavior orchestration, factor out common logic across different tasks

  • Implement component tests and telemetry/metrics collection pipelines

  • Identify technical debt early enough to guide the team toward sustainable solutions

  • Act as the go-to person for software quality: modern C++ practices, code structure, error handling, robustness. Likewise for Python.

    • Configuration & tooling

  • Design an easily extensible and testable module for deploying policies that can be reused across tasks and supports schema versioning for observations, so a deployed policy pins the exact version of the computations it was trained against

  • Provide technical leadership on C++ and Python tooling (clang-tidy, sanitizers, static analysis, linting, typing, test setup)

  • Work with our incoming simulation team to unify training, benchmarking and evaluation tooling across tasks, so adding a task doesn't mean forking tooling and infrastructure


    • What we're looking for

    Required

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Robotics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field

  • 5+ years developing complex C++ systems, with deep knowledge of modern C++ (17 and onwards)

  • Strong Python for tooling, configuration and simulation-side scripting

  • Strong experience designing large, modular software systems that outlived their first use case

  • High standards for software quality and long-term maintainability

    • Nice to have

  • Experience with behavior trees, state machines, or other task orchestration frameworks in production

  • Experience working alongside learned controllers in a production stack - deployment, versioning, observation pipelines. No need to train them.

  • Motion planning, geometric algorithms, or spatial data structures

  • Feature-flagged deployments, staged rollouts, or long-lived platforms


    • This role is a great fit if…

  • You want to make systems work reliably in the real world, and enjoy thinking through the edge cases

  • You'd rather our next behavior be a configuration than a dedicated piece of software

  • You want the best idea to win regardless of who had it, and you'd rather be corrected by the numbers than agreed with

  • You take a result end-to-end: when something needs to happen, you use or ask for whatever it takes, even outside your scope

  • You're a software purist, but pragmatic — first make it work, then make it right, and cut corners consciously when it's the right call

    About Share

    Share is the global marketplace for bandwidth. We aggregate telco infrastructure across Africa (fiber routes, subsea capacity, data centers, cloud on-ramps) into a single intelligence layer. That lets ISPs, hyperscalers and AI companies get connectivity where they need it in seconds, not months.

We're replacing that with one neutral exchange: an API on top of real infrastructure, with prices set by actual supply and demand. It's already live across East Africa, with thousands of kilometers of fiber, 12 infrastructure providers, 10 data centers, and around 8 million people served.

    The Role

    Our network is the foundation of the product. Every route a customer provisions through our API has to exist, perform and stay up on real hardware. We're hiring a Senior Network Developer to design and build that network as software: a distributed, multi-provider fabric that engineers change through code, not by logging into devices.

    You'll own the network architecture end to end. That covers our BGP edge (transit, peering at KIXP and LINX, private interconnects with hyperscalers), the backbone, and the PoPs and data centers we're adding across the continent. You'll set the standards our network is built to, which partner ISPs connecting to us will inherit. As we grow, you'll also help build the network engineering team.

    What you'll do

    • Design the backbone and PoP architecture as standard, repeatable building blocks, from edge to data center, so we can add capacity and new markets without redesigning each time.

    • Drive our move to Segment Routing and a clean IP architecture, including IPv4 reuse, IPv6, and how customer and internal address space coexist.

    • Build on disaggregated white-box hardware (Edgecore with IP Infusion OcNOS today), and make the hardware and software calls that keep us fast and affordable.

    • Turn operations into software. That means a source of truth (Nautobot), templated config (Jinja), and CI/CD with validation, staged rollouts and rollback for every change.

    • Build the telemetry and observability that show what the network is really doing. Use AI where it actually helps: anomaly detection, automated triage, and auto-remediation with a human in the loop.

    • Own availability. Limit how much any failure can affect, mitigate first and diagnose second, and turn post-mortems into fixes in the system.

    • Work with our software team on the API and provisioning layer that exposes the network to customers, and with partner ISPs' engineers on the hand-off.

    • Help hire and develop the engineers who'll run this with you.

    Our Ideal Candidate

    • 8+ years building and operating large networks at a hyperscaler, CDN, internet exchange, carrier or ISP.

    • Deep BGP at scale: route policy, communities, RPKI, traffic engineering, peering and transit.

    • Strong data center and backbone design. You know Clos/EVPN-VXLAN fabrics and MPLS or Segment Routing, and when each makes sense.

    • Hands-on with white-box or disaggregated networking, including choosing hardware and knowing where the silicon limits you.

    • You think like an owner. You bring ideas, not tickets, and you want to help build a team, not just a network.

    Competitive salary and meaningful equity in a venture-backed company (US-incorporated, with a Kenya operating entity)

    Network Operations Engineer

    1. About the role

    Share is the global marketplace for bandwidth. We aggregate telco infrastructure into a single layer and give ISPs, hyperscalers, and AI companies a clean path to deliver connectivity into every home and business across Kenya and the continent. Behind that marketplace is a real network: a BGP edge peering with Tier 1 transit, hyperscalers, and local exchanges, an MPLS backbone, aggregation and access gear, and the systems that watch all of it.

    For the partners who run on us, the network is the product, and the NOC is where they feel it. A clean shift is a partner who never knew anything happened. That is the bar.

    We are early and the team is small, so we cannot afford a pair of hands that only knows how to escalate. We need a capable network engineer who can stand a shift, resolve real faults without waking anyone, and then keep building the network while East Africa sleeps: propagation and peering checks, health passes across the estate, config changes through to merge, tickets off the board, automation that takes the next repetitive job off everyone's plate. The watching is the floor of this role, not the ceiling.

    The NOC you would be joining is not a legacy one. We are building it as an AI assisted operations environment from the ground up. The forwarding plane runs on open source routing and forwarding software, every device configuration lives in Git, and an LLM layer sits on top of the live network state. When something moves, that layer reads the telemetry, correlates it against the topology and the config history, and puts a probable cause and a candidate fix in front of the engineer on shift. The point is not to replace your judgment. It is to collapse the time between an alert firing and you knowing where to look, so mean time to repair is measured in minutes.

    You sit inside that system. You use it, you push back on it when it is wrong, and what you catch that it misses is part of how it gets smarter. As we build automation out across the NOC, you are not just a consumer of the tooling. You help write it.

    2. What you'll do

    Watch, and know what you're looking at. Sit on our monitoring stack (Zabbix and Grafana dashboards, flow telemetry, alerting) and actually read it. Learn what normal looks like so abnormal jumps out at you: a BGP session that dropped, a link that went down, latency climbing on a path, a capacity threshold breached, a partner suddenly pushing or pulling nothing.

    Troubleshoot and resolve. This is where you earn your seat. Confirm the alert is real, gather the facts, and localise the fault: one peer or many, us or upstream, a real outage or a monitoring blip. The assistive layer surfaces a likely diagnosis and a suggested fix, the config history is right there in Git, and the runbooks are live. Your job is to read all of it critically, decide what is actually true, and close out what you can on your own. Every ticket you resolve yourself is one our senior people did not get pulled out of deep work, or out of bed, to deal with.

    Keep the network healthy, not just alive. A quiet shift is not an idle one. Run the proactive passes: check that routes are propagating the way they should, that RPKI and filter chains are doing their job, that peering and transit sessions are clean across the edge, that no PoP is drifting toward a capacity wall. Catch the slow degradations that never trip an alert. The day team should inherit a network in a known good state.

    Build and automate. The repetitive parts of this job should not stay repetitive. Write the scripts that turn a manual check into a scheduled one. Push our config automation forward (Jinja driven generation, NAPALM or NETCONF/gNMI against the devices) so changes ship from data, not from memory. When the assistive layer keeps missing the same thing, that is a candidate for automation, and you are well placed to build it during the hours nobody else is online.

    Move the work forward. You are part of the network team, working the same board they do. Pick up tickets from the Linear queue, take config changes through review to merge, and keep our source of truth (Nautobot) accurate as the estate changes. Real work lands while East Africa is offline, so the team wakes up further ahead than they went to bed.

    Report exactly what is happening. For everything you cannot or should not fix alone, the handoff has to be clean: what is wrong, where, since when, what is affected, whether it is getting worse, and what you have already tried. No guessing dressed up as fact. No "the internet is down." A clear, written incident note a senior engineer can act on the moment they open it, and a tidy handover to the East Africa team at the end of your shift.

    Escalate well. Know the ladder cold: what you are cleared to touch, what you must not touch alone, and who to bring in for what. Escalating early on a genuine outage is good judgment. Sitting silently on a problem because you were unsure is the one thing that gets people out of bed angry. Handle what you can, raise the rest fast and clearly, and do not turn either dial too far.

    3. Who we're looking for

    A network engineer who can stand on their own through a shift, and who treats the quiet hours as time to build rather than time to wait. You will not be the most senior engineer on this team, and you do not need to be. The people you escalate to are CCIE level. What we need from you is independence and range: work a problem properly, resolve a fair share of it yourself, and use what is left of the shift to actually move the network forward. Pair that with clear reporting, sound judgment about when to bring in help, and the instinct to question a machine's suggestion rather than follow it blindly, and you are who we are looking for.

    Must-have

    • Strong networking competence, held in your hands rather than on paper. CCNA and well beyond it. You understand TCP/IP, routing and switching, IP addressing and subnetting, DNS, DHCP, NAT, and how they behave when they go wrong.

    • Real troubleshooting instinct. Given a degraded link or a dropped session, you know where to look and what to rule out. You can read BGP session state, follow a path with ping and traceroute, and tell a local fault from an upstream one without waiting to be told.

    • Working BGP knowledge. Reading communities and route policy, spotting a flap or a leaky origin, understanding how transit, peering, and RPKI behave at the edge.

    • Comfortable on the gear and the CLI. Linux, network device CLIs, and dashboards are familiar ground. We run MikroTik (RouterOS) across the network and so do many partners, so RouterOS experience is a real plus.

    • Comfortable working with config in Git. Configuration lives in repos, not on devices. Reading a diff, understanding why a config changed, and proposing one yourself should not be foreign to you.

    • Some scripting, and the appetite to do more. Bash or Python, enough to automate the repetitive parts away and to grow into our config and automation pipelines. We are not hiring a button pusher.

    • Clear written English. You can describe a technical situation accurately and briefly so someone picking it up cold understands it instantly.

    • Calm under pressure and dependable. When the graphs go red you get more precise, not more panicked. You show up for every shift, alert and on time.

    • Located in New Zealand or a nearby time zone where covering our deep overnight maps onto your normal working day.

    Nice-to-have

    • CCNP, or MikroTik MTCNA / MTCRE.

    • Prior NOC, ISP, or carrier operations experience.

    • Hands on with MPLS (L3VPN, EVPN) and the multi-tenant isolation a shared backbone needs.

    • Exposure to open source and white box routing or forwarding stacks (SONiC, IP Infusion OcNOS, FRR, or similar).

    • Network source of truth and automation tooling (Nautobot, NAPALM, Jinja config generation, NETCONF or gNMI).

    • Familiarity with a monitoring stack such as Zabbix, Grafana, Loki, or Prometheus, and with flow telemetry.

    • Working familiarity with FreeRADIUS, CoA and Disconnect flows, and how session control and accounting hook into the network.

    • Exposure to applying ML or AI in network operations: anomaly detection, predictive failure analysis, automated triage or remediation.

    • IPv6 and dual stack exposure, and internet exchange operations (looking glass and route server behaviour, IRR and RPKI hygiene).

    4. What we offer

    • A seat inside a serious, very senior network team, with people who have deep service provider backgrounds and will sharpen you fast. You will see how a real carrier network behaves under live conditions.

    • A front row seat to how a network actually gets run in 2026. Open source forwarding, config as code, and an LLM layer doing real operational work. Not a slide about the future of network operations, but the environment you would work in every shift, and help build.

    • Real engineering, not just monitoring. The role is built so the quiet hours go into automation, propagation and health work, and tickets off the board. The path into deeper network engineering and automation work is the plan, not a vague someday.

    • Competitive salary and private health and wellness benefits, fully remote, in a mission driven, investor backed company building the backbone of Africa's next generation internet.

CT Marketing Agency is seeking skilled Freelance Copywriters to write high-quality, SEO-driven content for eCommerce and lead generation websites. This is a freelance, project-based writing role.

 

The ideal candidate has excellent English writing skills, strong research ability, and experience writing content that follows detailed, client-specific guidelines. Projects commonly include category pages, product descriptions, blog posts, SEO landing pages, and website copy.

Our client base is constantly evolving, and writers may create content across a wide range of industries, including:

  • Complete assignments by deadline and communicate professionally with the team

Qualifications

  • 2 to 4 years of professional, non-academic writing experience preferred
  • Strong understanding of SEO writing best practices
  • Ability to research unfamiliar industries and technical topics
  • Ability to write creative, engaging, accurate, and ROI-focused content
  • Portfolio featuring published work preferred
  • Experience in specialized industries strongly preferred

Compensation

Writers are paid on a per-word basis. Rates are assessed according to our KPI rubric.

Initial compensation is up to $0.06 per word, with $0.034 per word being the most typical rate

This equals approximately $30 or $17 per 500-word page

After 400 live pages, the top rate increases to $0.064 per word, with $0.038 per word being the most typical rate

After 800 live pages, the top rate increases to $0.07 per word, with $0.044 per word being the most typical rate

 

Application Process

Candidates should be prepared to provide a portfolio featuring published work. Once an offer is extended, writers will complete a brief training course.

First and most importantly: our mission is to bring transparency and clarity to the world's data.

Our platform, Voxel51, is where AI work happens. Our enterprise platform is the mission critical linchpin for managing unstructured data, model development, and AI systems at the world's largest companies.

We believe that open source is the way to lead the data-centric AI revolution. FiftyOne, our open source version of Voxel51 has 5 million downloads to-date.

Our software massively impacts AI work across almost every vertical: from self-driving cars to medical imaging to revolutionizing agriculture, we are at the thrilling center of real-world AI advancement’s next wave.

And we’re built on three key tenets:

  • We are all human beings: we strive to be a “human-first” organization and treat everyone with the respect, care, and flexibility that all people deserve.
  • We are distributed: we believe in getting autonomy and power into the hands of people actually doing the work.
  • We believe in the power of community.

We are fully remote, hiring for someone in the United States.

About Your Role
As a Robotics Developer Relations Engineer at Voxel51, you'll work directly in the Voxel51 community — answering technical questions, building integrations with robotics perception stacks, models, and datasets, creating engaging technical content, and helping organize and speak at events (in-person and virtual). This role is ideal for someone who has worked hands-on with robotic systems and wants to help the broader robotics ML community build.

What You Will Do
  • Technical Support: Provide technical answers to Voxel51 users on Slack, StackOverflow, and Reddit — including questions from robotics engineers working on real-world deployment challenges
  • Writing: Author original blogs, tutorials, and documentation at the intersection of robot learning and data infrastructure (VLAs, world models, sim-to-real pipelines)
  • Videos: Self-produce short videos for social media and long-format videos exploring technical topics relevant to robotics practitioners
  • Educational Content: Create and deliver original courses, both online and in-person, covering computer vision and ML topics for robotics applications
  • Integrations: Code integrations that combine FiftyOne with complementary technologies, models, and datasets used in robotics — including simulation environments, sensor data formats, and perception frameworks
  • Events: Help organize community events like Meetups and hackathons, and speak at in-person and virtual conferences/workshops focused on robotics and autonomous systems

Examples:

  • Technical integration and blog:
  • Community Q&A:
  • Video:
  • Educational Content:

What You Should Bring

  • 3+ years of professional ML experience, with direct experience applying computer vision to robotics systems (e.g., perception, navigation, manipulation, or autonomous vehicles)
  • MS or PhD in computer science, robotics, or a related field, with an emphasis on computer vision
  • Hands-on experience with robotics-specific data types and tools — e.g., multimodal sensor streams like MCAP/LeRobot and simulators like Isaac Sim
  • Proficiency with Python
  • Expertise with machine learning and scientific computing libraries (TensorFlow, PyTorch, NumPy)
  • Great writing ability and proficiency with a screen recording/editing suite
  • Links to blogs, articles, or papers written — bonus for robotics-focused content
  • Links to conferences or events you have spoken at — bonus for robotics/autonomy-focused events (e.g., ICRA, IROS, CVPR workshops)
  • Links to open source communities where you are an active participant (robotics-related projects a plus)
  • Links to GitHub repos where your code is visible
  • Ability to work in a remote-first, cooperative environment using collaborative development tools (GitHub, Slack)

Compensation


The cash compensation for this role is in the $190K–$240K range. In addition to base compensation, we offer equity in the form of options, a variety of benefits, and the opportunity to grow in an exciting, collaborative environment.

About SH/FT

Shift Paradigm is an execution-led strategic consultancy that bridges the gap between enterprise strategy and technical reality. We partner with Fortune 500 brands and emerging leaders to solve the inherent complexity of modern digital marketing. As partners to the world’s leading MarTech platforms, including Adobe, Salesforce, Optimizely, and Braze, we deploy integrated experts across data analytics, marketing strategy, technology development, engineering, and revenue operations to ensure our clients’ tech stacks don't just exist, but perform.

Location: Remote, US, EST time zone

The Role

As Director of Email Development & QA, you will lead a team of 10-15 developers and QA specialists delivering pixel-perfect campaigns for our Fortune 100 financial services client. You will own the production ecosystem—driving efficiency, automation, and 100% SLA compliance—while collaborating to translate business strategies into scalable technical architectures. This role also involves pre-sale scoping and leading the integration of AI within our workflows.

This role reports directly to our SVP, Managing Director.

What You’ll Accomplish

Business Leadership and Team Development

  • Directly manage a team of 10-15 FTEs and contractors, in North America and offshore, overseeing recruiting, performance management, and career development.
  • Establish technical standards and engineering culture to ensure high-quality, reusable code based on responsive design systems.
  • Architect and optimize the end-to-end development pipeline to maximize resource utilization and profitability.
  • Partner with cross-functional leads to ensure accurate project scoping, resourcing, and timely delivery.

AI-Native Practice Leadership

  • Bring a clear, informed point of view on how AI is changing email development, delivery workflows, and what it means for how a professional services team should be structured and operate.
  • Lead the integration of AI-assisted development tools, code generation, testing automation, and other AI-enabled workflows across the team.

Client Delivery and Technical Oversight

  • Architect, document, and continuously optimize the end-to-end development-to-QA pipeline; eliminate workflow redundancies, automate manual tasks, and champion production-line efficiency.
  • Along with our Senior Creative Director, oversee the governance, maintenance, and scalability of the agency’s fully responsive modular email design systems and template frameworks.
  • Connect abstract data requirements to advanced technical solutions, acting as the senior authority on complex personalization logic, API frameworks, custom scripts, and platform capabilities (e.g., Salesforce Marketing Cloud).
  • Own the quality and integrity of developer and QA output across client engagements, from scoping decisions through to deployment.
  • Partner with client, project and delivery leads to ensure work is scoped correctly, resourced appropriately, and delivered on time.
  • Provide hands-on technical guidance and escalation support on complex or high-risk deliverables.
  • Maintain visibility across active engagements to identify risk early and keep delivery on track.
  • Track, analyze, and enforce strict compliance with internal and client-facing Service Level Agreements (SLAs).
  • Act as the ultimate technical safety net; intercept execution failures and deliverability roadblocks to diagnose root causes and implement agency-wide improvements.

Scoping, Resourcing & Burn Management

  • Participate in pre-sale conversations to assess development requirements, translate business needs into technical scope, and develop accurate level-of-effort estimates.
  • Identify opportunities to build reusable frameworks, accelerators, and development assets that improve delivery speed and consistency across engagements.
  • Understand the broader financial landscape of client retainers; flag out-of-scope development requests and balance resource costs (internal vs. contractor spend) to maximize delivery profitability.

What You Bring

Experience & Expertise

  • 10+ years in email engineering, with 4+ years leading technical teams in an agency or consulting environment.
  • Expertise in Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Adobe Journey Optimizer, and rendering tools like Litmus or Email on Acid.
  • Proven ability to scope custom development, contribute to Statements of Work (SOWs), and manage stakeholder expectations regarding timelines and complexity.
  • Expert communicator capable of leading technical discussions with all audiences, from developers to C-Suite executives.
  • Strong operational understanding of email accessibility requirements and best practices.
  • Broad fluency across email development, front-end development, back-end systems, API design, systems integration, and cloud infrastructure (AWS, Azure, etc.)
  • Experience evaluating, piloting, or implementing AI-native development practices within a team or organization.

What We Offer

  • Competitive compensation aligned with your experience and impact.
  • Remote flexibility.
  • Collaborative culture that values diverse perspectives and innovative thinking.
  • Work that makes a measurable difference for your clients.

Why SH/FT:

SH/FT is a consultancy built for transformation. We bridge the gap between marketing, data, and technology to unlock growth for some of the world’s most recognized brands. As Director of Engineering and Development, you will shape how our clients build and scale technology solutions, lead a team of talented engineers doing genuinely complex work, and have a real voice in how SH/FT’s engineering practice grows and evolves.

Comp & Benefits

As required by law, SH/FT provides a reasonable range of compensation for roles that may be hired in California, Colorado, Hawaii, New York, New Jersey, or Washington. The salary range for these residents is $165,000 to $185,000 + annual performance based bonus. Salary is based on several factors including but not limited to scope of responsibilities, skillset, relevant experience, certifications, and more.

In addition to base salary, SH/FT offers benefits such as medical, dental, vision, STD/LTD, Life/AD&D, Flexible Paid Time Off, and various other ancillary benefits and perks.

We welcome and encourage applications from people with disabilities. Accommodations are available on request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process.

Candidates must have current U.S.work authorization. This employer participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S.

No relocation assistance can be offered at this time.

All inquiries are held in strict confidence.

Ameresco, Inc. (NYSE: AMRC) is a leading energy infrastructure company delivering integrated solutions that provide reliable power and modernize infrastructure. Since 2000, we have served as a trusted partner to public and private sector customers across North America, the UK and Europe, delivering over $15 billion in solutions and contracting more than 5 GW of energy resources.

At Ameresco, we integrate energy resources and modernize the built environment through innovative infrastructure solutions that improve reliability, optimize performance, strengthen resilience, and support long-term sustainability. Join us in building the infrastructure that powers the future. Explore opportunities to make a meaningful impact while growing your career with a company at the forefront of energy innovation.


Position Overview:

Ameresco is hiring a Senior Project Manager to lead two to three solar PV, distributed generation, community solar, and battery energy storage system (BESS) projects concurrently, depending on project size, phase, and complexity. You will coordinate with Business Development and Preconstruction during project development and turnover, then lead execution from Notice to Proceed through construction, commissioning, commercial operation, and final closeout. The role combines remote project leadership with regular site presence during critical construction, commissioning, and recovery activities and is accountable for safety, schedule, cost, quality, commercial outcomes, and client communication.


This is a hands-on senior project delivery role that combines direct project ownership with cross-functional leadership and mentoring of Project Managers and Assistant Project Managers. This role reports to the Senior Director of Construction – Solar PV & BESS with a preference for candidates located in the Greater Boston area with the ability to work from the Boston office periodically based on business and team needs. Remote U.S. candidates may be considered for the right fit and will be expected to travel to the Boston office quarterly.

Responsibilities:

  • Partner with Business Development and Preconstruction to review contract requirements, estimate assumptions, baseline schedules, procurement, permitting, interconnection, constructability, site logistics, staffing, and subcontractor strategy, then convert the sold project into an executable plan with clear scope, budget, schedule, risk ownership, and decision paths before mobilization.
  • Lead assigned solar PV, distributed generation, community solar, and BESS projects from Notice to Proceed through commercial operation and final closeout.
  • Manage procurement and subcontractor performance, including scope alignment, commitments, deliverables, schedule compliance, field coordination, and issue resolution.
  • Direct cross-functional project teams that include Construction Managers, Superintendents, Engineering, Procurement, Safety, Quality, project controls, subcontractors, OEMs, and support staff.
  • Manage project budgets, forecasts, contingency, cash flow, and margin, and drive value-engineering opportunities with Engineering and Procurement.
  • Lead project-level change-order development, negotiation, claims support, schedule recovery, and management of liquidated-damages exposure; escalate material commercial and contractual risks to Commercial, Legal, and senior leadership.
  • Maintain the baseline schedule, evaluate critical-path impacts, develop recovery plans, and hold internal teams and contractors accountable for commitments.
  • Serve as the primary day-to-day client contact, coordinate with utilities and developers, communicate decisions and risks clearly, and resolve or escalate issues before they affect project outcomes.
  • Coordinate testing, commissioning, energization, turnover, and applicable BESS, electrical, fire-code, permitting, prevailing-wage, apprenticeship, and certified-payroll requirements with the responsible internal teams, OEMs, consultants, utilities, and authorities having jurisdiction.
  • Drive commercial operation and final closeout, including punch-list completion, documentation, training, warranties, final account reconciliation, and resolution of remaining exposure.
  • Provide accurate, decision-ready project reporting to the Senior Director of Construction, including safety, cost, schedule, procurement, quality, commercial exposure, key decisions, and required support.
  • Mentor Project Managers and Assistant Project Managers, reinforce consistent project controls, and share practical lessons learned across the construction team.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Construction Management, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant construction experience.
  • Minimum of 10 years of construction project management experience.
  • Minimum of 5 years supporting solar PV, BESS, distributed generation, community solar, or related power infrastructure projects.
  • Experience managing projects valued from $5M to $150M+.
  • Strong command of EPC/EPCM delivery, subcontract management, and construction execution.
  • Proven commercial skills: change-order negotiation, claims management, and cost forecasting.
  • Experience leading or mentoring project managers.
  • Proven ability to manage projects, teams, and contractors remotely, with strong written communication.
  • Willingness to travel 20–30% to assigned project sites; valid driver's license required.

Additional Qualifications:

  • Direct utility-scale solar construction experience, including project execution through commissioning and closeout.
  • Utility-scale BESS construction and commissioning experience, including OEM coordination and energization.
  • Working knowledge of NFPA 855, UL 9540/9540A, NFPA 70E, and NEC, with AHJ/fire-department permitting experience.
  • Experience with applicable IRA prevailing-wage and apprenticeship requirements, including certified-payroll documentation.
  • Utility interconnection experience (e.g., ISO-NE, PJM, MISO).
  • PMP and/or PE; OSHA 30; NABCEP a plus.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Project, Procore, and other construction management software.

The anticipated base salary range for this role is $134,000 - $194,000 (presented in good faith). In addition to base pay, employees receive a comprehensive benefits package, such as health insurance, retirement plans, and paid time off, and may be eligible for performance incentives, bonuses, commissions, or equity, depending on the role.

Actual pay will depend on factors such as internal equity, skills, experience, education, certifications, and location. This range supports our commitment to pay transparency and compliance with applicable laws. Compensation may vary by work location, including remote arrangements.

We disclose salary ranges and benefits in all required external and internal postings and will provide further details upon request at any stage of the hiring process. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis until the position is filled.

Ameresco challenges the brightest, most talented, and creative individuals in the industry by providing an environment that fosters initiative and achievement. We are proud of our comprehensive and competitive employee benefits, including people-oriented insurance, investment, and incentive plans.

All official communications from Ameresco will originate from an @ameresco.com email address. Any correspondence from other domains should be regarded as fraudulent. Please report any suspicious activity to the platform where the issue was encountered. For further inquiries or concerns, please contact us at 1-866-AMERESCO

Ameresco is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

Meet Aperture

At Aperture, we create value and drive growth by delivering exceptional product consultancy and advertising services to our global partners.

Through data-driven strategies, we combine performance marketing, creative strategy, product optimisation, CRM, analytics and experimentation to help ambitious companies scale.

Founded in 2022 by Hannah Parvaz, Aperture has quickly made waves. Already recognised as Business Consultant of the Year and named 2024’s Most Innovative Growth Agency, we’re now building the team that will take us into our next stage of growth.

We work with some of the most exciting apps, platforms and digital products in the world. Our job is not just to make things look good. Our job is to make growth happen.

Our culture

  • Growth mindset. We’re hungry to learn and improve.
  • Take full responsibility for every outcome. No excuses.
  • Obsess over results. We’re here to make a measurable impact.
  • We’re data-obsessed. We let numbers, not opinions, guide our decisions.
  • Client success is our success. Period.
  • No ego. The best idea wins, regardless of who it comes from.
  • Radical candour. We give and receive honest feedback to fuel growth.
  • No job is too small. We support each other and JFDI.

Work from anywhere

We’re remote-first and impact-first.

Work from wherever you’re most productive, while staying closely connected to the team through regular collaboration, team sessions, client work and in-person meetups.

We also bring the team together for retreats, events, conferences and working sessions around the world. Travel to team meetups is covered.

You must be able to work in a UK timezone.

The role

We’re hiring a Video Editor to create brilliant, high-performing content for our clients and Aperture.

You should be chronically online, in the best possible way.

You know what people are watching, sharing and talking about. You spot emerging formats before every brand starts copying them. You understand why a video holds someone’s attention, when an edit feels native and when something feels too polished, too slow or painfully corporate.

You’ll turn raw footage, creator content, product recordings, AI-generated assets and creative concepts into paid social ads and organic content that people actually want to watch.

AI-native. Human-led.

This is an AI-native creative role, but it is fundamentally human-led.

We're not looking for people who can generate content. We're looking for tastemakers: editors with exceptional judgement who know what feels fresh, what feels native and what people actually want to watch.

AI expands what's possible, but taste is what makes the work valuable. The tools will keep changing; your eye for storytelling, internet culture, pacing and creative direction is what sets the standard.

If you're the person sending references before everyone else has seen them, spotting formats before they become trends, and pushing ideas beyond the obvious, you'll fit right in.

Requirements

What you’ll do

  • Edit paid social ads, UGC, creator content and short-form organic videos.
  • Turn raw footage into compelling stories with strong hooks, pacing and structure.
  • Create multiple versions of concepts to test different openings, messages, formats and lengths.
  • Add captions, music, sound design, graphics, transitions and motion where they improve the work.
  • Adapt videos for TikTok, Reels, Meta, YouTube Shorts and emerging platforms.
  • Use generative video, image, voice and audio tools to create, transform and extend creative assets.
  • Combine AI-generated scenes with creator footage, product recordings, motion graphics and traditional edits.
  • Experiment with tools such as Luma, Runway, Kling, Veo and whatever emerges next.
  • Develop repeatable AI workflows that increase the speed, range and ambition of our creative output.
  • Keep up with trends, creators, sounds, memes, editing styles and wider internet culture.
  • Bring relevant references and proactive ideas into creative discussions.
  • Work closely with creative strategists, designers, performance marketers and creator managers.
  • Use performance results to improve future edits and iterate on winning ideas.
  • Share new tools, techniques and creative possibilities with the wider team.
  • Keep projects, source files and versions organised across multiple accounts.

You’ll be great at this if

  • You have a strong portfolio of short-form video work.
  • You understand how to earn attention within the first few seconds.
  • You have an instinct for pacing, storytelling, humour, tension and timing.
  • You can edit quickly without the work feeling careless.
  • You understand the visual language of TikTok, Instagram, Meta and YouTube.
  • You know the difference between using a trend well and arriving after it is already dead.
  • You’re confident using Premiere Pro, After Effects, CapCut or similar tools.
  • You’re already experimenting with AI creative tools and can show us what you’ve made.
  • You understand that prompting is only one part of the process; taste, direction, editing and iteration are what make the output good.
  • You can recognise and correct the inconsistencies, artefacts and visual clichés that make AI-generated content feel cheap.
  • You’re excited by how quickly creative technology is changing and actively teach yourself new workflows.
  • You can take inconsistent or imperfect footage and find the strongest possible edit.
  • You take feedback well, move quickly and aren’t precious about your work.
  • You care about how your work performs, not just how it looks.

Experience editing performance ads, UGC or creator-led content is a strong advantage, but exceptional social-first work matters more than a particular background.

This is not the role for you if

  • You don’t spend much time on social platforms.
  • You only want to work on polished brand films or long-form productions.
  • You need every shot and transition mapped out before you can begin.
  • You prefer perfecting one video to producing and testing multiple strong versions.
  • You’re interested in making beautiful videos but not whether people watch or act on them.
  • You have no interest in using AI as part of your creative process.
  • You treat AI as a shortcut for weak ideas, poor craft or generic content.
  • You’re uncomfortable receiving frequent, direct feedback.

What success looks like in six months

  • Our videos feel current, native and distinctive.
  • Strong concepts are being turned into multiple testable edits quickly.
  • Winning hooks, structures and formats are being identified and iterated.
  • Editing is increasing the speed and quality of our creative output.
  • AI is meaningfully increasing the range and ambition of what we produce without reducing its quality.
  • You have introduced repeatable AI-assisted workflows that the wider creative team can use.
  • Performance learnings are consistently influencing new work.
  • The team trusts you to bring ideas, spot opportunities and deliver excellent work.

Benefits

  • Work from anywhere, with flexibility around how you structure your day.
  • Direct exposure to high-growth clients and meaningful work.
  • Regular team meetups and retreats, with travel covered.
  • Access to conferences, events and industry sessions.
  • Small team, high ownership and fast progression.

Before you apply

We read every application.

Show us the work that best represents your editing style, particularly short-form content, paid social, UGC or creator-led videos. Include anything you have created or enhanced using AI.

If you haven’t yet used AI extensively, tell us what you’re experimenting with and what you would be excited to create.

We’ll also ask a few questions about what you’re watching, what you think is working and how you approach an edit.

Specific, honest answers matter far more than polished ones. We can tell when something is generic.

As a Sustainability Program Manager, you will build relationships and collaborate with domestic and multinational food companies (restaurant chains, caterers, retailers, hospitality groups, and packaged good companies) to help them incorporate sustainable foods such as plant-based ingredients into their supply chain.

Globally, a growing number of companies are adopting or considering plant-based food policies and commitments as part of their sustainability initiatives. Major corporations in the hospitality, food service, and retail sectors have started to incorporate plant-based options to reduce their environmental impact. The shift is driven by increasing consumer demand for sustainable and ethical food options, along with companies' efforts to meet their ESG goals.

In this role with Lever Foundation, you will help educate more companies on the sustainability, animal welfare, and economic benefits of making this supply chain shift. You will provide industry updates, connect these companies with potential suppliers, and provide other resources to help them understand and make progress on the issue. In order to identify and engage new food companies, you will do online research, write and send emails, make calls, and conduct visits and meetings with companies.

You'll work from home and hours are highly flexible. You'll have wonderful colleagues in Asia, Europe, and the US who will work with and support you. You’ll stay in close touch with them through calls, email and messages.

Through this work you will have hands-on experience working with large food companies on corporate sustainability, with room for advancement to managerial or other positions.

We do not require any particular educational or work background; instead, we're looking for a candidate with the specific personality traits and skills needed to succeed in this job:

  • Excellent interpersonal communication skills, with the ability to persuade and engage others
  • Ability to work highly independently, with a very strong work ethic
  • Resiliency — when you are ignored or brushed off, it does not discourage you but rather motivates you to try harder
  • Excellent verbal and written English and Tagalog
  • Personal interest in sustainability or animal welfare

Calling all ambitious, personable individuals who want a job with meaning! Want a full-time job working from home (some travel required) at a job that makes the world a better place? Set your own full-time hours, with room for growth, competitive salary and a results-driven atmosphere. This is a great job for productive, self-directed people who are highly skilled at interpersonal communication, who are resilient, and who want to do work that makes a difference. Must be fluent in English and Tagalog.

Lever Foundation is a US-based charity that works to promote food sustainability and animal welfare. In the sustainable food sector, we work with large food companies, providing them with professional consulting services to help them add sustainable food to their supply chains, thereby improving food safety and food quality, and improving animal welfare. Our partners include main food and beverage chains Burger King, Starbucks, Jollibee Food Group, Andok's, Figaro Coffee Group, Max's Group, Shakey's, SM Retail, Robinsons, etc.

It’s More Than a Career, It’s a Mission.

Our people are the foundation of our success. By joining our growing team at Sarah Cannon Research Institute (SCRI), a subsidiary of McKesson, you will have the opportunity to become part of one of the largest community-based cancer programs to advance oncology treatments and improve outcomes for cancer patients across the globe. We look for mission-driven candidates who have a desire to advance the fight against cancer and make a difference in the lives of patients diagnosed with cancer every day.

Our Mission

People who live with cancer – those who work to prevent it, fight it, and survive it – are at the heart of every decision we make. Bringing the most innovative medical minds together with the most passionate caregivers in their communities, we are transforming care and personalizing treatment. Through clinical excellence and cutting-edge research, SCRI is redefining cancer care around the world.

Our Research Quality Manager is responsible for implementing the quality assurance program, managing and performing consult/support visits at investigative sites, assisting with onsite external audits and inspections, and providing routine quality support for assigned investigative sites.


This is a remote position in the US; relocation assistance and visa sponsorship are not available.


Duties include but are not limited to:

  • Develops and maintains effective relationships with investigative sites and other SCRI departments and colleagues
  • Monitors and modifies policies and procedures
  • Utilizes quality tools that assess the quality indicators of study operations
  • Monitors quality indicators for all sites using Risk-Based approach and within framework of QBD – Quality by Design - and prioritizes quality indicators depending on severity/urgency
  • Identifies areas of deficiency in quality and reports those deficiencies to SC Directors and other appropriate colleagues
  • Assists the business in development and modification of process documents
  • Assists with preparation and hosting of external audits
  • Assists research staff in maintaining regulatory compliance
  • Performs process / focused audits (as needed) of research sites utilizing research audit tools to ensure quality and reports audit findings to the appropriate leadership.
  • Ensures timely and appropriate follow-up in areas of deficiency.
  • Communicates observations and deficiencies to the Site Director / Manager and study PI, as appropriate.
  • Assists sites with Root Cause analysis and responses to external audits and CAPAs.
  • Maintains records of audits and reports.
  • Communicates with monitors and auditors of clinical trials, as needed.
  • Educates staff in quality improvement methods and industry trends
  • Other duties as assigned

Qualifications needed

  • Bachelor’s Degree required, Master’s Degree preferred
  • Minimum 3 years’ work experience in Quality Assurance, Quality Management, or Quality Auditing preferably in a clinical research, healthcare or life sciences field
  • Expertise in GCP, FDA and other applicable regulations in a risk-based environment

About Sarah Cannon Research Institute

Sarah Cannon Research Institute (SCRI) is one of the world’s leading oncology research organizations conducting community-based clinical trials. Focused on advancing therapies for patients over the last three decades, SCRI is a leader in drug development. In 2022, SCRI formed a joint venture with former US Oncology Research to expand clinical trial access across the country. It has conducted more than 850 first-in-human clinical trials since its inception and contributed to pivotal research that has led to the majority of new cancer therapies approved by the FDA in the past decade. Job Description:

Who We Are:

We’re Cart.com, one of the fastest growing commerce enablement companies in the world. We provide the digital and physical infrastructure that empowers thousands of leading B2C, B2B and public sector organizations to unify commerce operations from product discovery to product delivery.

We’re building toward a world where commerce has no bounds. Our enterprise-grade software, services and logistics infrastructure, including our own network of omnichannel fulfillment and distribution centers, enable merchants to navigate an increasingly complex operating landscape and drive efficient growth.

Our goal is to be the global backbone of commerce. To achieve it, we’re looking for entrepreneurial, innovative and determined teammates who are eager to help our growing base of customers simplify their commerce operations and seamlessly reach their own customers, wherever they are. Sound like you? We’d love to hear from you.

Cart.com Fast Facts:

  • 6,000+ customers worldwide
  • 1,600+ employees globally
  • 17 warehouses nationwide, totaling over 10 million square feet of space
  • Headquartered in Houston, TX with international offices in Mexico and Poland

Our values:

Cart.com is building a company that is committed to living out these 6 core values:

  • Be brand obsessed: Our lives are shaped by the brands we interact with daily. We obsess over the brands we serve, and about the things they care about.
  • Think beyond the box: “We’ve always done it that way” is not a phrase uttered often at our office. We create creative solutions to complex problems.
  • Don’t give up: We learn from our challenges and see them for what they are; great building blocks to an amazing brand story.
  • Speak up: We communicate clearly and directly because we care deeply. Communication is the bedrock of our community.
  • Work together: We’ve built a team that prides itself on diversity of thought and background. Collaboration is better with contrast.
  • Remember to be human: We work hard, but we leave room for the people, places and things that we love.

AI is part of how we work. It’s not doing the hiring.

We'll use AI in parts of our process and we think you should feel free to use it too — for research, prep, whatever helps. But our interviews exist to meet you, not your best AI-assisted draft. Real people make every call here. Any questions about how this works, just ask.

Remote:

This position is open to applicants or individuals who are located in or willing to move to AL, AZ, CA, CO, CT, DE, FL, GA, IL, IN, IA, KY, LA, ME, MD, MA, MI, MS, NE, NV, NJ, NY, NC, OH, OR, PA, SC, TN, TX, UT, VA, WA, WV.


The Role:

The Merchant of Record (MoR) Accountant will provide end-to-end ownership of Cart.com’s Merchant of Record accounting operations. This role is responsible for the integrity and accuracy of payment processing, settlements, tax compliance, financial reconciliations, and operational controls across MoR brands.

The ideal candidate is highly detail-oriented, thrives in a fast-paced environment, and combines strong accounting fundamentals with payments operations expertise. This individual will serve as the primary accounting and operational owner of the MoR process, helping scale the business while maintaining robust financial controls and compliance standards.


What You’ll Do:

Merchant of Record Operations & Financial Oversight

  • Own the accounting and operational oversight of Merchant of Record activities across supported brands.
  • Review, validate, and approve high-value transactions and settlements in accordance with established approval thresholds and internal controls.
  • Monitor and resolve urgent payment exceptions, including settlement failures, payment holds, chargebacks, and significant refunds.
  • Maintain rigorous transaction-level review processes to minimize errors, prevent revenue leakage, and ensure financial accuracy.
  • Serve as the primary liaison for payment processing, settlements, reconciliations, tax compliance, and financial reporting related to MoR operations.

Reconciliations & Financial Controls

  • Perform and oversee reconciliations between payment platforms, banking activity, operational systems, and the general ledger.
  • Investigate and resolve discrepancies in a timely manner, with clear documentation of root cause and resolution.
  • Support month-end close activities, including journal entries, account reconciliations, and reporting.
  • Continuously improve control processes and identify opportunities for automation and operational efficiency.

Tax & Compliance

  • Ensure accurate sales tax collection, remittance, and reporting across applicable jurisdictions.
  • Manage tax configurations and coordinate with internal and external partners to maintain compliance.
  • Support audits and regulatory inquiries related to payment operations and Merchant of Record activities.

Process Improvement & Documentation

  • Develop, maintain, and enhance accounting policies, operational procedures, and internal controls.
  • Partner with payment providers and external vendors to support contractual compliance and operational effectiveness.
  • Implement and maintain statements of work, contracts, and operating requirements with payment vendors.
  • Create and maintain playbooks, standard operating procedures, and process documentation to support scalability and knowledge transfer.

Who You Are:

  • Exceptionally detail-oriented, with a consistent commitment to accuracy and rigorous transaction review.
  • A sound decision-maker who exercises strong judgment under time pressure.
  • Able to act with urgency while maintaining compliance, risk management, and financial controls.
  • Highly organized and capable of managing competing priorities in a rapidly changing environment.
  • Comfortable operating with ambiguity and driving issues through resolution.
  • Demonstrates integrity, accountability, and strong financial stewardship.

What You’ve Done:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Business, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
  • Three to seven years of experience in payments operations, merchant services, accounting, finance, or a related field within e-commerce, SaaS, digital goods, marketplace, or technology-enabled services.
  • Strong understanding of payment processing, settlements, merchant accounts, and financial controls.
  • Hands-on experience preparing reconciliations, journal entries, and month-end close support.
  • Advanced Excel skills and experience analyzing large datasets.
  • Working knowledge of SQL and reporting or analytics tools.

Nice to Haves:

  • Prior experience supporting or operating a Merchant of Record model or managing MoR vendors and platforms.
  • Experience with payment platforms such as Stripe, Braintree, PayPal, or similar providers.
  • Familiarity with tax automation solutions such as Avalara, TaxJar, or comparable systems.
  • Experience with ERP platforms such as Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central, NetSuite, or similar applications.
  • Experience developing scalable procedures, automation, and controls within a high-growth/fast paced environment.

  • Lead large-scale projects from ideation through enterprise impact.
  • Apply a broad problem-solving toolkit to develop both creative and practical solutions.
  • Evaluate trade-offs between out-of-the-box and customized solutions, optimizing for speed and effectiveness.
  • Implement scalable, bug-free, and well-tested solutions that reduce complexity rather than add to it.
  • Understand business challenges and deliver results that meaningfully solve key problems.
  • Proactively engage with stakeholders across all levels to align data science efforts with business needs.
  • Identify and mitigate risks early, preventing roadblocks that could arise later.
  • Serve as a trusted advisor and thought partner, ensuring projects are delivered on time and aligned with business objectives.
  • Mentor and collaborate with peers, improving team-wide problem-solving capabilities and technical execution.

Success in this role looks like:

  • First 90 Days:
    • By your ability to forecast project impact.
    • By leading data driven product performance assessment.
  • Beyond 90 Days:
    • Proactive identification and implementation of strategic improvements with data driven strategies.
    • By leading toward improved team outcomes.

You should get in touch if:

  • You have an advanced degree in a quantitative field (Master’s + 3-4 years of experience or Ph.D. + 2+ years of experience).
  • You have a strong foundation in probability, statistics, and machine learning tools, including SQL, Python, and relevant ML/statistical packages.
  • You have successfully used data science to drive enterprise value in a business function.
  • You are comfortable leading projects and have experience taking large-scale initiatives from concept to measurable business impact.
  • You improve the work of those around you through mentorship, code review, and leadership by example.
  • You can clearly communicate how your work contributes to business goals, ensuring alignment with top-level company objectives.

Benefits Overview:

  • Financial Well-Being: Our commitment to attracting and retaining top talent begins with a competitive base salary and equity opportunities. Additionally, we offer a performance-based bonus program, 401k matching, and regular compensation reviews to recognize and reward exceptional contributions.
  • Physical Well-Being: We prioritize the health and well-being of our employees and their families by providing comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage. Your health matters to us, and we invest in ensuring you have access to quality healthcare.
  • Mental Well-Being: We understand the importance of mental health in fostering productivity and maintaining work-life balance. To support this, we offer initiatives such as No-Meeting Fridays, monthly company holidays, access to mental health resources, and a generous flexible time-off policy. Additionally, we embrace a remote-first culture that supports collaboration and flexibility, allowing our team members to thrive from any location.
  • Professional Development: Developing internal talent is a priority for Clover. We offer learning programs, mentorship, professional development funding, and regular performance feedback and reviews.

Additional Perks:

  • Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP) offering discounted equity opportunities
  • Reimbursement for office setup expenses
  • Monthly cell phone & internet stipend
  • Remote-first culture, enabling collaboration with global teams
  • Paid parental leave for all new parents
  • And much more!

About Counterpart Health: In 2018, Clover Health set out to do something unprecedented: build a clinically intuitive, AI-enabled solution that fits within physicians' workflows to help support the earlier diagnosis and management of chronic conditions.

Years later, that vision is a reality, with thousands of practitioners using Counterpart Assistant during patient visits to improve disease management, reduce medical expenses, and drive success in value-based care.

With an exceptional team of value-based care and technology experts, Counterpart Health is driving value-based care at the speed of software.

Counterpart Health is a subsidiary of Clover Health. From Clover’s inception, Diversity & Inclusion have always been key to our success. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and our employees are people with different strengths, experiences, perspectives, opinions, and backgrounds, who share a passion for improving people's lives. Diversity not only includes race and gender identity, but also age, disability status, veteran status, sexual orientation, religion and many other parts of one’s identity. All of our employee’s points of view are key to our success, and inclusion is everyone's responsibility.

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records. We are anE-Verify company.

Final pay is based on several factors including but not limited to internal equity, market data, and the applicant’s education, work experience, certifications, etc.

A reasonable estimate of the base salary range for this role is:
$176,900—$230,000 USD

      <title>Customer.io: Contract Accounts Payable Manager</title>
      <region>Anywhere in the World</region>
      <category>Full-Stack Programming</category>
      <description>

<p>
  <strong>Headquarters:</strong> Americas Remote
</p>

<h3>About <a href="http://customer.io/">Customer.io</a></h3>
<p>Over 9,000 companies — from scrappy startups to global brands — use our platform to send billions of emails, push notifications, in-app messages, and SMS every day. <a href="http://Customer.io">Customer.io</a> powers automated communication that people actually want to receive. We help teams send smarter, more relevant messages using real-time behavioral data.</p>
<h3>About the role</h3>
<p>Hi, my name is Eric Anderson, Senior Controller at <a href="http://Customer.io">Customer.io</a>, and I'm looking for an AP Contractor to keep our T&amp;E engine running clean through a busy stretch. Our Accounting team relies on Ramp and Navan to keep expense and travel spend moving, and we need someone who can own the day-to-day grind — coding, reconciling, chasing exceptions — without losing sight of the bigger picture. This is a 6-month contract with real ownership from day one, working closely with Terre Holmes and the AP team.</p>
<h3>What we value</h3>
<ul>
<li><strong>Ownership</strong> — you drive the exception queue to zero, not someone else.</li>
<li><strong>Directness</strong> — you enforce policy clearly and kindly, without dodging hard conversations.</li>
<li><strong>Precision</strong> — a mismatched dollar amount doesn't get past you.</li>
</ul>
<h3>What you’ll do</h3>
<ul>
<li>Own Ramp expense management end-to-end — review, code, and approve expense reports, chase missing receipts, and enforce policy compliance.</li>
<li>Administer Navan travel — reconcile bookings and spend, flag policy exceptions, and support employees through out-of-policy approvals.</li>
<li>Review AP bills for accuracy, coding, and approval routing — catching duplicate invoices and mismatched amounts before they hit the payment queue.</li>
<li>Reconcile Ramp and Navan activity against the GL and drive the exception queue to zero before every close.</li>
<li>Serve as the responsive point of contact for vendors — confirming payment details, tracking status, and resolving disputes.</li>
<li>Spot recurring T&amp;E headaches and propose (and document) process fixes.</li>
</ul>
<h3>What we're looking for</h3>
<ul>
<li>3+ years of AP &amp; T&amp;E experience, ideally in SaaS or a high-growth environment</li>
<li>Hands-on experience with Ramp and/or Navan (or comparable — Concur, Expensify, TravelPerk)</li>
<li>Sharp eye for detail and a solid grasp of expense policy enforcement</li>
<li>Excellent written and verbal communication skills</li>
<li>Ability to manage a recurring, deadline-driven workload</li>
<li>Experience with NetSuite or a comparable ERP is a plus</li>
</ul>
<h3>Compensation &amp; Benefits</h3>
<p>This is a contracted engagement at <strong>$45–60/hr USD</strong>, depending on experience, for an estimated 6-month term.</p>
<h3>Our Process</h3>
<p>No gotchas, no trick questions - just a clear, human process designed to help both of us make an informed decision.</p>
<ol>
<li>30-minute video call with a Recruiter</li>
<li>45-minute video call with the Hiring Manager</li>
<li>45-minute cross-functional screen with a member of the AP team</li>
</ol>
<p>All final candidates will be asked to complete a background check and employment verifications as part of our pre-employment process.</p>
<p><a href="http://Customer.io">Customer.io</a> recognizes the stifling impact of systemic injustice on diverse communities. We commit to using our influence to increase inclusion and equity within the tech industry. We strive to build an inclusive team culture, implement bias-free hiring practices, and develop community partnerships to expand our global impact.</p>
<p>Zoom is the only video conference platform that we use, virtual interviews will be conducted using the video capability (i.e., not via the chat), and offers will be extended in writing on official <a href="http://customer.io/">Customer.io</a> letterhead. Please be vigilant in all of your job search activity, and if you have any questions please contact <a href="mailto:jobs@customer.io">jobs@customer.io</a>.</p>
<h3>Join us!</h3>
<p>Check out our&nbsp;<a href="https://customer.io/careers/">careers page</a>&nbsp;for more information about why you should&nbsp;<a href="https://customer.io/about/">come work with us!</a> We believe in empathy, transparency, responsibility, and, yes, a little awkwardness. If you’re excited by what you read — apply now.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p><strong>To apply:</strong> <a href="https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/customer-io-contract-accounts-payable-manager">https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/customer-io-contract-accounts-payable-manager</a></p>
</description>

      <region>Anywhere in the World</region>
      <category>Full-Stack Programming</category>
      <description><img src="https://we-work-remotely.imgix.net/logos/0171/6433/logo.gif?ixlib=rails-4.0.0&w=50&h=50&dpr=2&fit=fill&auto=compress" />

<p>
  <strong>Headquarters:</strong> Minnesota
    <br /><strong>URL:</strong> <a href="https://www.steuartnutrition.com/">https://www.steuartnutrition.com/</a>
</p>

<p><strong>About us</strong></p>
<p>Steuart Nutrition is a GMP-certified contract manufacturer making powders, liquids, capsules and stick packs for growing wellness brands. We run on Extreme Ownership, clear communication and fast turnaround, and we want a developer who works the same way.</p>
<p><strong>The role</strong></p>
<p>We're hiring a remote developer to own the customization of our training app. You'll learn the platform quickly, then build what our teams need to train and onboard people. Over time you'll also take on other internal tools and automations. AI-assisted development is central to how we work, so we want someone who uses AI tools to write and ship better code faster.</p>
<p><strong>What you'll do</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Learn our training app inside and out, then customize and extend it</li>
<li>Build features, integrations and automations with AI coding tools like Claude, Cursor, Copilot and Grok</li>
<li>Turn rough requests from the plant and office teams into working solutions</li>
<li>Document your work so others can use it and maintain it</li>
<li>Give regular, clear progress updates</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>What we're looking for</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>3+ years of professional software development</li>
<li>Strong, proven skill with AI-assisted coding: you know how to prompt, check and fix AI-generated code</li>
<li>A track record of quickly learning unfamiliar platforms and codebases</li>
<li>Experience with APIs, web apps and integrations (JavaScript/TypeScript or Python preferred)</li>
<li>Excellent written English and consistent communication</li>
<li>Able to overlap at least 4 hours a day with US Eastern Time</li>
<li>Bonus: experience with LMS or training platforms, or with manufacturing or regulated industries</li>
</ul>

<p><strong>To apply:</strong> <a href="https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/steuart-nutrition-software-developer-ai-coding">https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/steuart-nutrition-software-developer-ai-coding</a></p>
</description>
